subject: Re: Renewal and capacity conversation — Novabiz benchmarking
messages:
From: Cassandra Jones <cassandra.jones@novabiz.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@novabiz.com, Alex Romero <alex.romero@novabiz.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal window + benchmarking with competitor

Hi Vivek / Vanessa,

We’re starting renewal planning for our LLM infrastructure (renewal due end of Aug). We just completed an internal bakeoff with a vendor (Competitor.ai) and they’re pushing pricing that would let us consolidate two of our clusters — that’s a material cost delta for us.

Quick summary: performance is comparable on our 8k token prompts, Competitor.ai showed 15% faster p99 on our reranking workloads, and they offered a 20% blended TCO reduction if we move fully to them (they quoted a one-year discounted commit).

Before we spin up any final procurement conversation, can Redwood run a short benchmark against the exact workload we used (reranking + few-shot generation) and share a succinct comparison? Also: we’d like to understand what it would take to increase dedicated capacity by ~30% for Q4 if we decide not to move.

We’d like to keep this low-friction and avoid an escalation, so if you can send a mutual action plan and a test plan we can share with our infra team, that’d be helpful.

Thanks,
Cassandra
Cassandra Jones
Head of ML Infrastructure, NovaBiz
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Cassandra Jones <cassandra.jones@novabiz.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window + benchmarking with competitor

Cassandra —

Thanks for the heads up and level setting. We can absolutely run an apples-to-apples benchmark against your reranker/generation mix. I’ve copied Ben (solutions) and Vanessa (AM) — Ben will take the lead on the bench and Vanessa will land the procurement/term-side conversation.

Immediate next steps:
- Ben: will run the benchmark using your workload (can we get the test corpus + sample prompts you used?)
- Vanessa: will draft a short mutual action plan and propose a renewal cadence
- I’ll assemble a short save package: a one-page capacity plan, a 12-month commercial option with a dedicated buffer, and a suggested discount structure for a renew+expand commitment.

Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow (Thu) to align on scope and timelines? If tomorrow doesn’t work, early next week is fine.

– Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window + benchmarking with competitor

Vivek / Vanessa —

I have enough to start with based on Cassandra’s note but need the test corpus + a short sample of your production prompt mix to match the bakeoff. If you can get that to me (or give S3 read access for a 48-hr window) I’ll:

1) Run the reranker + generation workload across the current Novabiz model pin (v2.3) and the recommended quantized variant, and the competitor config where possible.
2) Capture p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-thousand-tokens for steady-state and burst scenarios.
3) Produce a single-page summary + a 2-slide deep-dive for your infra team.

Deliverable ETA: 48 hours after I get the corpus. I’ll attach the benchmark template I’ll use.

Attachments: capacity_plan_q3.xlsx (spreadsheet, 48KB)

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@novabiz.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Cassandra Jones <cassandra.jones@novabiz.com>, procurement@novabiz.com
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 10:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window + benchmarking with competitor

Ben / Vivek —

Thanks — attaching the corpus and a short note on the prompt mix. We’ve also included the competitor logs and the bakeoff spreadsheet so you can replay their numbers.

Attachments: novabiz_corpus_subset.tar.gz (archive, 12MB), novabiz_prompt_mix.csv (CSV, 12KB), competitor_bakeoff_logs.zip (archive, 900KB)

Alex
Platform Ops, NovaBiz
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@novabiz.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Novabiz benchmark summary (first pass)

Alex / Cassandra / Vivek / Vanessa —

Attached is a first-pass summary of the benchmark run against the exact corpus/prompts you provided. High level:
- Redwood (v2.3, quantized variant) matched Competitor.ai on median latency and exceeded them on p99 (we’re ~12% better p99 on the reranker workload).
- Cost-per-1k tokens (steady-state): Redwood is ~8% higher without a committed discount; with a 12-month committed profile at your expected volume, we can match or beat their blended TCO.
- Burst capacity: Redwood’s autoscaling consistently sustained the short spikes in your test; we recommend a 30% dedicated buffer for Q4 to remove risk during peak campaigns.

Deliverables attached: novabiz_benchmark_summary.pdf (PDF, 92KB), mutual_action_plan.docx (DOCX, 34KB)

Next steps I recommend:
1) Share the one-page summary with the infra team (attached).
2) Vanessa/Finance propose a commercial option: a 12-month renew+30% capacity commit with a blended discount (tiered by usage).
3) We can offer a 60-day dedicated buffer trial (no-change to your routing) to give you operational confidence.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk the slides. If we proceed with the 12-month commit, Procurement, please tell us your signature authority and DocuSign contact.

—Ben
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Cassandra Jones <cassandra.jones@novabiz.com>, Alex Romero <alex.romero@novabiz.com>, procurement@novabiz.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Novabiz benchmark summary (first pass) — proposal and next steps

Cassandra / Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Ben — the bench looks good and I appreciate the clarity. To keep this moving and avoid disruptive procurement cycles, here’s a concise offer we can present to leadership this week: 

Offer summary:
- 12-month renewal with a 30% dedicated capacity increase for Q4 (committed monthly minima).
- Commercial: 15% committed discount off list with a performance credit structure (up to 5% back if p99 latency exceeds the agreed SLO on a monthly basis).
- 60-day dedicated buffer trial starting Sept 1 at no additional setup fee; if you choose to return to shared capacity after trial, we’ll invoice only for usage.
- Upfront: standard 30-day payment terms + DocuSign signature.

Vanessa will follow with a short mutual action plan and a formal DocuSign. Procurement — if you can confirm signatory and preferred CLM, I’ll get legal working on the smallest-possible SOW to move this to signature.

If this sounds OK, we can aim to get something in Procurement’s hands by Tue 2027-08-03.

— Vivek
Senior Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: mutual_action_plan.docx (DOCX, 34KB), novabiz_benchmark_summary.pdf (PDF, 92KB)
